editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the DSST Organizational Behavior exam covering individual behavior, group dynamics, structure, motivation, leadership, and culture with detailed.
editorial.overview: The DSST Organizational Behavior exam assesses knowledge of workplace behavior, managed by DSST. It features a total of 100 multiple-choice questions administered in a convenient computer-based format. Candidates must achieve a passing score of 400 to earn academic college credit recommendations, making targeted preparation important for success on test day. The standard registration fee is set at $85 for civilians, while eligible military personnel can take the assessment for free through DANTES funding. You will have a total duration of 120 minutes to complete all items.
editorial.who_should_take: Students seeking college credit for organizational behavior coursework, military personnel utilizing DANTES benefits, and adult learners aiming to demonstrate professional management competencies through standardized testing.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review core textbooks and academic resources aligned with organizational psychology and management theory. Focus your study efforts extensively on employee motivation theories, leadership styles, group behaviors, and structural frameworks. Take multiple practice assessments to build accurate pacing and confidence for the computer-based testing format within the designated duration.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain carefully covers individual behavior within the workplace, focusing specifically on psychological factors, perception mechanisms, learning processes, and various employee attitudes that directly influence overall professional performance outcomes on the test.

This domain carefully examines group dynamics, team development stages, communication patterns, conflict resolution methods, and the interactive processes that significantly shape team productivity and collaboration in corporate environments.

This domain focuses heavily on organizational structure, design elements, bureaucracy, and how various structural frameworks directly impact operational efficiency, communication channels, and daily workflow across enterprises during evaluations.

This domain explores core motivation theories and drive mechanisms that heavily influence worker effort levels, goal-setting behaviors, and overall performance outcomes within various organizational settings covered during the evaluation process.
study_focus: Content and process theories of motivation

domain_guidance.summary: This domain addresses specific leadership theories, behavioral approaches, power dynamics, and political strategies utilized by managers to effectively guide teams toward achieving strategic business goals within modern workplace environments.

This domain investigates organizational culture, shared core values, socialization processes, and how cultural environments profoundly affect employee behavior, retention, and long-term institutional success across various professional corporate settings today.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the computer-based testing center with proper identification. Manage your time across the multiple-choice questions so that all items receive a response before the duration expires.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam consists of a total of 100 multiple-choice questions delivered in a computer-based format. Candidates answer all items within the designated testing time to successfully complete the evaluation process.
The minimum passing score required to successfully complete the exam is 400. Meeting this score earns you valuable college credit recommendations for your academic transcript.
The exam has a strict duration of 120 minutes. Candidates must complete all multiple-choice questions efficiently within this specified time frame to ensure every item receives a response.

faq.question_title: How much does the exam cost?
faq.answer_text: The standard fee for civilians taking the exam is $85. Eligible military members can take the test entirely for free via established DANTES funding programs.
